name: The Haven · Tucson
description: The Haven describes residential and outpatient treatment for women, trans women, and non-binary or gender-nonconforming people assigned female at birth. Its FAQ states that participants must be 18 or older.
Residential treatment includes living at the treatment campus. Admission, assessment and payment arrangements are handled by The Haven.
limitation: This is a treatment service. Historical treatment outputs or facility capacity do not establish a current residential opening, ordinary rental housing, eligibility or admission.

name: Where to get shelter help in Surprise
service_type: Housing navigation and shelter referrals · Surprise
description: Native American Connections runs the West Valley Housing Assistance Center at 12779 W. Grand Ave. in Surprise. It lists housing navigation and assessment help Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Phoenix Rescue Mission operates eight shelter units for families at the site but handles shelter eligibility and intake off-site. Families with children under 18 can call the Family Housing Hub at 877-211-8661. For single adults, the operator lists the Brian Garcia Welcome Center in Phoenix at 602-229-5155.
limitation: Check the operator’s current instructions before going. The center’s resource hours are not walk-in shelter intake hours, and eight units is not a vacancy count.

name: What a motel stay can mean for shelter eligibility
service_type: Federal shelter-definition reference · Phoenix & Maricopa County
description: Federal homelessness definitions generally include a motel stay paid for by a charity or government program as emergency shelter. Maricopa County’s future provider solicitation also allows hotel or motel vouchers when congregate emergency shelter is unavailable.

name: Marana: School help when housing is unstable
service_type: School enrollment, stability and transportation · Marana Unified
description: If your family is staying with others because you lost housing or are facing financial hardship, or living in a motel because you have no adequate alternative, your student may qualify for McKinney-Vento school support. In Marana Unified, call 520-616-3013 and ask for the district’s McKinney-Vento liaison. Ask about enrolling right away, staying at the same school when it’s in the student’s best interest, and arranging transportation.
limitation: This is school support, not a housing or shelter placement referral.
